10901.full:
Σπανία, -ας, ἡ
(= cl. Ἑσπερία or Ἰβηρία; late writers adopted the Roman name, Ἱσπανία (1Ma.8:3) or Σ. as here),
Spain: Rom.15:24, 28.†
(AS)

s: associated with or pertaining to the flesh, fleshly, carnal
in a more ethical sense, of the nature of the flesh, under the control of its appetites, fleshly, carnal, sensual
10902.full:
σαρκικός, -ή, -όν (σάρξ)
(seel. for σάρκινος, Arist., H.A., x, 2, 7)
= Lat. carnalis, i.e.
__(a) associated with or pertaining to the flesh, fleshly, carnal: Rom.15:27, 1Co.9:11;
__(b) in a more ethical sense, of the nature of the flesh, under the control of its appetites, fleshly, carnal, sensual (but including more than mere sensuality; cf. Hort, 1Pe., 133): 1Co.3:3, 2Co.1:12 10:4, 1Pe.2:11.†
SYN.: σάρκινος (which see), ψυχικός; cf. Tr., Syn., §§ LXXi, LXXii; Lft., Notes, 184 f.; Vau. on Rom.7:14 (AS)

s: to strive together with, to help
10903.full:
συν-αγωνίζομαι
to strive together with, to help (prop., of sharing in a contest): with dative of person(s) and of thing(s), Rom.15:30.†
(AS)

10907.full:
Ἰουνίας, -α, ὁ
(or Ἰουνία, -ας, ἡ, Junia; AV, H, mg.)
Junias: Rom.16:7.†
(AS)

10908.full:
συν-αιχμάλωτος, -ου, ὁ
a fellow prisoner (prop., of a captive in war, see Lft., Col., 234): Rom.16:7, Col.4:10, Phm 23.†
(AS)

10914.full:
the narcissus , (Homeric Hymns), etc.
From ναρκάω, because of its narcotic properties. (ML)

10915.full:
Τρύφαινα, -ης, ἡ
Tryphæna: Rom.16:12 (see Lft., Phi., 175 f.; MM, xxv).†
(AS)

10916.full:
Τρυφῶσα, -ης, ἡ, ς, ἡ
Tryphosa: Rom.16:12 (see Lft., Phi., 175 f.).†
(AS)

10920.full:
Ἑρμᾶς, -ᾶ, accusative, -ᾶν (Doric form of Ἑρμῆς),
Hermas, a Christian: Rom.16:14.†
(AS)

10921.full:
1. fond of speaking , (Plato Philosophus)
2. fond of learning, literary , Lat. studiosus, (Aristotle Philosopher) (ML)

10923.full: Nereus , a sea-god, son of Πόντος (the sea) , father of the Nereids, (Hesiod) (ML)

10925.full:
χρηστολογία, -ας, ἡ
(χρηστός, λέγω),
fair speaking: in bad sense, Rom.16:18 (in good sense also, eccl.).†
(AS)

10931.full:
ἀγενής, -ές
(γένος),
__1. unborn (Plat.);
__2. of no family, ignoble, base (opposite to ἀγαθός, Soph., Fr., 105): opposite to εὐγενής, 1Co.1:28 (for exx. from π., see MM, VGT, see word).
† (AS)

s: by the aid of the Holy Spirit
10933.full:
πνευματικῶς
adv. (πνεῦμα),
spiritually;
__(a) by the aid of the Holy Spirit: 1Co.2:13 (WH, mg.), 1Co.2:14;
__(b) in a spiritual sense : Rev.11:8.†
(AS)

10934.full:
ἐπ-οικοδομέω, -ῶ
in NT, always metaphorically, of the spiritual life regarded as a building (Cremer, 449);
__1. to build upon: 1Co.3:10 3:12 3:14; pass., Eph.2:20.
__2. to build up: Col.2:7, 1Pe.2:5 (T, οἰκοδ- WH, Rec.), Ju 20.†
(AS)

s: to be puffed up with pride
10935.full:
φυσιόω, -ῶ
(φῦσα, bellows), = cl. φυσάω,
to puff or blow up, inflate. Metaphorical, to puff up, make proud: 1Co.8:1. Pass., to be puffed up with pride: 1Co.4:18-19 5:2 13:4; before ὑπό, Col.2:18; before ὑπὲρ . . . κατά, 1Co.4:6 (on the form of the subjc., see M, Pr., 54; Bl., § 22, 3).†
(AS)

10936.full:
συμ-βουλεύω
[in LXX chiefly for יָעַץ ;]
__1. to advise, counsel: with dative of person(s), Jhn.18:14; id. before inf., Rev.3:18.
__2. Mid., to take counsel, consult: before ἵνα, Mat.26:4 ("reciprocal middle," see M, Pr., 157); with inf., Act.9:23.†
(AS)

10938.full:
γυμνιτεύω (Rec. γυμνητ-, V. Tdf ., Pr., 81),
to be naked or scantily clad: 1Co.4:11 (cf. ἐν ψύχει κ. γυμνότητι), 2Co.11:27; γυμνοί, Jas.2:15. In κοινή writers, γ. also means to go light-armed.†
(AS)

s: to be unsettled, be homeless, lead a vagabond life
10939.full:
ἀστατέω, -ῶ
(ἄστατος, unstable), [in Aq.: Isa.58:7 (LXX, ἄστεγος)* ;]
to be unsettled, be homeless, lead a vagabond life (Cremer, 738 MM, see word): 1Co.4:11 †
(AS)

10940.full:
παιδαγωγός, -oῦ, ὁ
(παῖς, ἄγω),
a guide, guardian, trainer of boys, a tutor (disting. from διδάσκαλος, Xen., Lac., 3, 1), usually a trusty slave: opposite to πατήρ, 1Co.4:15; figuratively, of the Law, π. εἰς Χριστόν, Gal.3:24-25.†
(AS)

10941.full:
μιμητής, -οῦ, ὁ
(μιμέομαι),
in NT always (like the verb) in good sense, an imitator: 1Co.4:16 11:1, Eph.5:1, 1Th.1:6 2:14, Heb.6:12.†
(AS)

10946.full:
ἐγκρατεύομαι, depon.,
[in LXX for אפק, Gen.43:31, 1Ki.13:12, Est.5:10 א 3 * ;]
to exercise self-control: 1Co.7:9; with accusative, πάντα (see Bl., 91), 1Co.9:25.†
(AS)

10947.full:
ἀπ-ελεύθερος, -ου, ὁ, ἡ
a freedman: τ. κυρίου (MM, see word), 1Co.7:22.†
(AS)

s: steadfast, firm; metaphorically, of moral fixity
10951.full:
ἑδραῖος, -ον (ἕδρα, a seat), [in Sm.: Ps 32 (33):14, al. ;]
__1. sitting, seated.
__2. steadfast, firm; metaphorically, of moral fixity: 1Co.7:37 15:58, Col.1:23.
† (AS)

s: an incision, a cutting, break. 2. Metaphorical, an interruption, a hindrance
10952.full:
ἐγκοπή, see: ἐνκ-.
ἐν-κοπή (Rec. ἐγκ-, see: ἐν; T, ἐκκ-), -ῆς, ἡ (ἐγκόπτω) ;
1. an incision, a cutting, break. 2. Metaphorical, an interruption, a hindrance: 1Co.9:12.†
(AS)

10953.full:
συν-μερίζω
(Rec. συμμ-), [in LXX: Pro.29:24 א2 (חָלַק) * ;]
to distri­bute in shares. Mid., to have a share in: 1Co.9:13 (Diod., al.).†
(AS)

10955.full:
βραβεῖον, -ου, τό
(βραβεύς, an umpire),
a prize in the games: 1Co.9:24; metaphorically, of the Christian's reward, Php.3:14.†
(AS)

s: to make a slave, bring into bondage
10958.full:
δουλαγωγέω, -ῶ
(δοῦλος, ἄγω),
to make a slave, bring into bondage: 1Co.9:27 (Cremer, 703).†
(AS)

10959.full:
κατα-στρώννυμι
[in LXX: Num.14:16 (שָׁחַט), Job.12:23 (שָׁטַח), שָׁטַח), Jdt.4.1-15; Jdt.2.1-28 Mac.4 ;]
__1. to strew or spread over.
__2. to lay low, overthrow: 1Co.10:5.†
(AS)

10960.full:
ἐπιθυμητής, -οῦ, ὁ
(ἐπιθυμέω) [in LXX: Num.11:34 (אָוָה hithp.); εἶναι ἐ., Pro.1:22 (חָמַד)* ;]
one longing for, lustful after: κακῶν, 1Co.10:6.†
(AS)

10964.full:
μάκελλον, -ου, τό (Lat. macellum),
a meat-market: 1Co.10:25 (see Deiss., LAE, 274; MM, xvi).†
(AS)

10965.full: (food) sacrificed to idols noun meat offered to an idol, 1Cor.10:28*

10968.full:
ἥσσων (Rec. ἥττ-, the Attic literary form), ἧσσων,
inferior, less; neut., τὸ ἧ., adverbially, less: 2Co.12:15; εἰς τὸ ἧ., for the worse (opposite to κρεῖττον): 1Co.11:17.†
(AS)

s: of the lord or master, imperial
10969.full:
κυριακός, -ή, -όν
(κύριος), [in LXX: κ. φωνη (Συριακή φ., R), 2Ma.15:36 A * ;]
__1. as frequently in Inscr. (LS, see word; Deiss., BS, 217 f.), of the lord or master, imperial.
__2. of the Lord (i.e. Christ): δεῖπνον, 1Co.11:20; ἡμέρα, Rev.1:10. (cf. λόγια κ., Papias, Eus., HE, iii, 39, 1; γραφαὶ κ., Clem. Alex., etc; for eccl. usage, cf. Soph., Lex., see word)†
(AS)

10970.full:
ὁσάκις
(ὅσος),
relat. adv.,
as often as: before ἐάν (which see), 1Co.11:25-26, Rev.11:6,†
(AS)

10972.full:
φανέρωσις, -εως, ἡ
(φανερόω), [in LXX as seel. for δήλωσις אוּרִים), Lev.8:8, Cod. Ven. (Thayer, see word) * ;]
manifestation: 1Co.12:7, 2Co.4:2.†
(AS)

10973.full:
ὄσφρησις, -εως, ἡ
(ὀσφραίνομαι, to smell),
the sense of smell, smell­ing: 1Co.12:17.†
(AS)

10975.full:
περπερεύοραι
(περπερος, vainglorious)
to boast or vaunt oneself: 1Co.13:4 (elsewhere. only in Antonin.; see Abbott, Essays, 87).†
(AS)

s: of alien speech, of another tongue
10977.full:
ἑτερό-γλωσσος
(Att.. -ττος), -ον, [in Aq.: Psa.114:1, Isa.33:19 * ;]
of alien speech, of another tongue (see Cremer, 681): 1Co.14:21 (aliter in LXX).†
(AS)

10980.full:
ἐλεεινός, -ή, -όν
(ἔλεος in Re, l.with, WH have the Attic poëtic form, ἐλεινός),
pitiable, miserable: Rev.3:17; comparat., 1Co.15:19.†
(AS)

10981.full:
θηριομαχέω, -ῶ
(θηρίον, μάχομαι),
to fight with wild beasts (Diod., al.): 1Co.15:32.†
(AS)

10984.full:
ἄ-τομος, -ον
(τέμνω), [in Sm.: Isa.54:8 (MM, see word) * ;]
indivisible; of time, ἄτομον, a moment: ἐν ἄ., 1Co.15:52.†
(AS)

10985.full:
ῥιπή, ῆς, ἡ
(ῥίπτω),
poët. in cl., any rapid movement such as the throw or flight of a javelin, the rush of wind or flame, the flapping of wings, the twinkling of lights; ῥ. ὀφθαλμοῦ, the twinkling of an eye: 1Co.15:52 (L, mg., ῥοπή, which see).†
(AS)

10987.full:
λογία
(prop., -εία, see BS, 142 ff.), -ας, ἡ (λογεύω, to collect, a word found in π., see Deiss., BS, l.with; LAE, 70, 103; MM, xvi),
a collection: 1Co.16:1-2.†
(AS)

s: a gentilic region in Asia Minor, settled by Gauls
A Roman Province which included this region
10988.full:
Γαλατία, -ας, ἡ,
Galatia;
__1. a gentilic region in Asia Minor, settled by Gauls (iii/B.C).
__2. A Roman Province which included this region (DB, ii, 85ff.): 1Co.16:1, Gal.1:2, 2Ti.4:10 (T, Tr., mg., Γαλλίαν), 1Pe.1:1.
† (AS)

10989.full:
ἐνεργής, -ές
(late form of ἐνεργός, on WH. cf. AR, Eph., 241),
at work, active, effective: 1Co.16:9, Phm 6, Heb.4:12 (Cremer, 261).†
(AS)

10990.full:
φορτούνατος (Rec. Φουρ-, see Mayser, 116 f.), -ου, ὁ
(Lat.) Fortunatus: 1Co.16:17 (see Lft., Cl. Ro., 1Co., 59).†
(AS)

10992.full:
μαρὰν ἀθά (Rec. μαραναθά; Aram.: on the original form see Dalman, Gr., § 41, 1; 74, 3; Words, 328),
Maranatha, i.e. the Lord cometh (but see Dalman, ll. with; Field, Notes, 180; ICC, in l): 1Co.16:22.†
(AS)

10993.full:
ἀπό-κριμα, -τος, τό
(ἀποκρίνω);
__1. prop., a judicial sentence: 2Co.1:9, R, mg.
__2. an answer (see Thayer, see word): 2Co.1:9, R, txt. (In FlJ, Ant., xiv, 10, 6, of a rescript of the Senate; in Inscr. of an official decision, Deiss., BS, 257; a reply to a deputation, MM, see word: cf. also Cremer, 3'75).†
(AS)

s: to help together, join in serving
10994.full:
συν-υπουργέω, -ῶ
to help together, join in serving: with dative instr., 2Co.1:11.†
(AS)

10995.full: to a greater degree; especially, frequently, extremely more, more abundantly, more earnestly, more vehemently, 2Cor. 7:13; exceedingly, extremely Gal. 1:14

s: to put a burden on, be burdensome
10998.full:
ἐπι-βαρέω, -ῶ
to put a burden on, be burdensome: figuratively, absol., 2Co.2:6; with accusative of person(s), 1Th.2:9, 2Th.3:8 (cf. M, Th., I, 29).†
(AS)

10999.full:
θριαμβεύω
(θρίαμβος, 1. a festal hymn to Bacchus. 2. The Roman triumphus),
__1. to triumph (and rarely, with accusative, to triumph over; so perh. Col.2:15, but see infr.).
__2. to lead in triumph: with accusative of person(s), 2Co.2:14; hence, generally, to make a spectacle or show of: Col.2:15 (but see supr.; cf. MM, Exp., xv; and esp. Field, Notes, 181).†
(AS)
